title: Rehire or Namesake? (Different SSN)
scenario_text: Peridot Labs' People Ops team is setting the service-tenure date for a benefits and vesting calculation. A worker in the current Workday system, employee E-90455 "Daniel R. Okafor," was hired 2022-08-15 as a Regular full-time software engineer, national ID (SSN) ending 6690. A legacy HRIS export (from a system retired in 2021) shows a prior worker "Daniel Okafor," employed as a full-time engineer from 2016-03-01 to 2020-11-30, national ID (SSN) ending 2214. Peridot's tenure policy states: for a rehired employee (the same individual returning to full-time employment), prior full-time service is bridged and counts toward the continuous-service date used for vesting, provided the break in service is under 5 years. If the two records are different people who merely share a common name, no bridging applies and tenure starts at the current hire date. The current Workday record's "prior service" field is blank because it was migrated without history. People Ops notes that name, job title, and even office location can coincide between distinct individuals, so the team is instructed to resolve identity strictly on the national ID before applying any bridging rule. HR must resolve whether the legacy record and the current record are the same individual, then set the continuous-service date accordingly. The break between 2020-11-30 and 2022-08-15 is under 5 years.
question: What continuous-service date should be used for Daniel Okafor's vesting calculation?
changed_fact: The national ID (SSN) on the legacy HRIS record changes from ending 6690 (matching the current Workday record, so both records are the same rehired person) to ending 2214 (a different person who shares the name). In the base the records resolve to one person whose prior service bridges; in the variant they are two different people and no prior service bridges.
